candidates_evaluated.name: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (IQ4_XS GGUF)
candidates_evaluated.disposition: not selected; GGUF deleted from ~/models/llm after this benchmark run

selection_rationale: All three candidates were run with identical settings (ctx-size 32768, n-gpu-layers 999, max_turns 40, per-task timeout per bench/llm/tasks.py, port 8099) per docs/llm/BENCHMARK.md. Only the 'script' class (5 tasks) can ever qualify under the >=5-task threshold, since 'test-writing' and 'mechanical-edit' each have only 4 tasks in the LLM-04 harness; those two classes are therefore never routed to the local model regardless of model or pass rate, independent of which candidate is picked. Among the three, Laguna-XS-2.1 had the best overall pass@1 (13/13, including a perfect 5/5 on 'script'), the lowest peak VRAM (16966 MB vs 18638/19102 MB, the most headroom under the 24 GB budget for coexistence with nnU-Net/MoveIt per config/llm_candidates.json), and a permissive license (OpenMDW-1.1). It is slower per task (wall time ~20-37s, ~105-130 tokens/s) than Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (~4-10s, ~145-155 tokens/s), and 3 of its 13 tasks (all test-writing) hit the max_turns=40 ceiling without the model calling 'finish' -- a tool-reliability caveat noted in docs/llm/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md even though the underlying artifact was still correct in all 3 cases. Qwen3-Coder was fastest but failed 2/13 tasks (84.6% pass@1, including the same script_case_id case-mapping bug Qwen3.6-27B also got wrong). Qwen3.6-27B was slowest (~35-39 tokens/s) and also missed script_case_id. Given REQ-LLM-1's selection dimensions (quantization, context, tool reliability, latency, license, VRAM coexistence), correctness (pass@1) and VRAM headroom were weighted highest since the local route exists to safely offload bounded coding tasks, not to win a speed contest; Laguna-XS-2.1 is the selection.
